title: Estimate critical behavior with feedback relay
equipment: Plate heat exchanger with qualified and deliberately weak feedback-relay copies
physicalPurpose: Estimate one critical frequency-domain point without manually increasing feedback gain toward instability.
objective: Execute and qualify a bounded feedback-relay experiment, reject an uninformative record, and derive one explicitly unapplied PI candidate.

simplifications: One local gain, dominant lag, and dead time
Ideal valve apart from declared amplitude bounds
Fixed flows, inlet temperatures, heat transfer, and fouling

baseline.limitation: Repeated manual gain changes near sustained oscillation are imprecise and potentially hazardous on physical equipment.

change.decision: Derive a candidate only when feedback-dependent cycles satisfy amplitude, noise, repeatability, limit, quality, and restoration criteria.

disturbances: Deterministic 0.05-degC measurement noise on both independent copies

acceptance.window: after two discarded transient cycles and before 180 s
upper and lower extrema over evaluation cycles
evaluation amplitude divided by 0.05-degC noise standard deviation
qualified evaluation amplitude compared with Lesson 42 reference
5th through 95th percentile over the enabled record
final sample after disable or timeout
final sample after disable or timeout

abortPredicates: Any required sample is stale, missing, forced, nonfinite, type-incompatible, or has bad quality
A valve command or temperature leaves its declared limit
A plant binding, sample interval, threshold, amplitude, seed, or restoration value changes
safety.restorationMode: Restore the relay amplitude request to 0 percent or reach the 180-second timeout, then confirm that both simulated valves return to 20 percent
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised process controls engineer and heat-exchanger operator
simulationOnlyRestrictions: This lesson cannot authorise physical relay excitation or gain application
Physical relay testing requires independent topology and hazard review, declared limits and interlocks, restoration proof, authorised roles, and explicit immediate approval

video.viewerOutcome: Recognise and qualify real feedback relay, reject a noisy record, and keep the derived candidate unapplied.

learning.context: Two independent simulated copies of the locally validated plate heat exchanger execute strong and deliberately weak feedback relays around the same operating point.
learning.reason: The preceding manual critical-gain experiment requires repeated operation near instability and should not become an unreviewed physical procedure.
theory: A feedback relay retains one of two bounded output levels and switches only when measured process value crosses a hysteresis threshold.
A repeatable limit cycle supports measured amplitude and period only after transient cycles, noise, limits, quality, and variation are qualified.
The symmetric-relay describing-function approximation estimates one critical point from relay amplitude and measured process amplitude.
Completing the experiment does not qualify the data, choose a controller, validate a candidate, or authorise application.
learning.workedPrediction: Predict 2/38 percent strong relay levels, 49.92/50.08 degC thresholds, period near 11.35 s, Ku in the region of 22.24 %/degC, and rejection of the 19.8/20.2 percent weak relay.
practicalPreparation: Verify Simulation evidence, accepted model scope, both independent plants, stable baseline, bindings, units, quality, timing, noise, thresholds, levels, limits, timeout, aborts, and restoration.
Record cycle, variation, amplitude-to-hysteresis, signal-to-noise, critical-gain, and no-application criteria before starting.
learning.baseline: Manual critical-gain search exposes dynamics but relies on repeated gain changes near sustained oscillation.
learning.change: Use measured-temperature threshold crossings to switch a bounded stateful relay and retain the complete record.
learning.comparison: Compare strong and weak records under equivalent conditions using cycles, amplitude, period, repeatability, signal-to-noise ratio, limits, and restoration.
learning.validation: Only the strong record may produce Ku and one historical PI candidate; the weak record must retain failed criteria and No tuning candidate.
learning.explanation: Lag and dead time sustain the feedback-dependent cycle, while hysteresis prevents noise chatter and qualification bounds the describing-function estimate.
learning.transfer: Relay automation does not replace eligibility, safety, data review, validation, or explicit application; Lesson 44 introduces model-based robustness-speed choices.
